references.text: Joseph's brothers slaughter a young goat and dip the robe in blood – the immediate preparation for the deception in verse 32.
Jacob recognizes the robe and mistakenly concludes that Joseph has been torn apart by a wild animal, showing that the brothers' deception succeeded.

Tamar sends items to Judah with the words 'Recognize them' (הַכֶּר־נָא), exactly the same expression the brothers used against Jacob. Judah, who deceived his father, is himself deceived with the same words.
Rebekah uses goat skins to deceive Isaac, a parallel to the brothers' use of goat blood to deceive Jacob – both involve deceiving a father through objects that hide identity.
Jacob gives Joseph the special robe (כְּתֹנֶת הַפַּסִּים), which is now used as evidence in the brothers' deception.
Proverbs speaks of the one who walks straight ahead as honest, while the crooked in their ways despises the Lord – a contrast to the brothers' dishonest deception of their father.
Parallel use of personal items for identification: Tamar uses them to reveal the truth, while Joseph's brothers use the robe to spread lies.
Powerful contrast: The robe in Genesis symbolizes lies and death, while the finest robe in Luke symbolizes truth and restoration.
